# Direction-adapted midpoint tails and the unused endpoint contribution

This note proves a directional shape constraint on an actual convex-body
midpoint coupling, an exact same-tilt identity, and a complete scalar formula
for cone projection profiles. It also gives an actual three-fiber example
showing that the previously selected centroid need not satisfy the asymmetric
OC bound. No general center-selection conclusion follows from the new shape
constraint alone.

Throughout, d>=1; A,B are convex bodies in R^d of volumes 0<a<=b; and

    v_*=((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d.

If a middle body K is used, it contains (A+B)/2 and has volume k. All
continuous halfspaces are closed. Their boundaries have zero volume for
these full-dimensional bodies and for all the coupling measures below.

## 1. A direction-adapted coupling with two concave tail roots

For each fixed u!=0 there is an actual measure eta_u such that

    eta_u(R^d)=a,    eta_u<=(a/v_*) dx,
    supp eta_u subset (A+B)/2,
    g_(eta_u)=(g_A+g_B)/2.                              (1)

For uniform probability on a body F, let

    F_u(t)=P[u.X>=t],
    Q_F(p)=the unique t with F_u(t)=p,  0<p<1.

Extend Q_F continuously to p=0,1 by the maximum and minimum support
values. Its strict monotonicity on (0,1) follows because every intermediate
slab through a full-dimensional convex body has positive volume. The
normalized directional upper quantile of eta_u is exactly

    Q_eta(p)=(Q_A(p)+Q_B(p))/2.                         (2)

Moreover both functions

    t -> [eta_u{u.x>=t}/a]^(1/d),
    t -> [eta_u{u.x<=t}/a]^(1/d)                       (3)

are concave on their respective full closed support intervals. The first
is decreasing and the second increasing. Concavity here is not asserted
after extending a vanishing tail by zero beyond its support.

Proof. Choose orthonormal coordinates with first coordinate u.x/||u||.
Apply the triangular conditional-quantile construction proved in
`accepted fact 486fe778f838d99d, f6641f09c19819a3`.
It sends uniform A to uniform B. In the first coordinate this is precisely
increasing quantile transport, so the two scalar projections are comonotone.
The midpoint of those projections has (2). The full midpoint map remains
triangular and injective. Its positive own-coordinate derivative product
is at least v_*/a, by the subset arithmetic-geometric-mean argument in
Section 1 of `candidate a972493c7a264f4e`.
Repeated one-dimensional substitution therefore proves the density bound
in (1), and support and vector first moment give its other assertions.
These dependencies prove an actual map and density statement, rather than
merely prescribing compatible scalar marginals.

For completeness, cap Brunn--Minkowski proves that F_u(t)^(1/d) is
decreasing concave on [min_F u.x,max_F u.x]. Indeed the Minkowski average
of two upper caps is contained in the cap at the averaged threshold.
The inverse of a decreasing continuous concave bijection is concave:
if f(x_j)=r_j, concavity gives f((1-lambda)x_1+lambda x_2)>=
(1-lambda)r_1+lambda r_2, and application of the decreasing inverse gives
f^(-1)((1-lambda)r_1+lambda r_2)>=
(1-lambda)x_1+lambda x_2. Thus

    r -> Q_A(r^d),  r -> Q_B(r^d)

are decreasing concave on [0,1]. Their average has the same property.
Taking its inverse proves the upper-tail claim in (3).

The same scalar comonotone coupling has lower quantile
Q_lower,eta(p)=(Q_lower,A(p)+Q_lower,B(p))/2: lower quantiles equal
the negatives of the corresponding upper quantiles for -u. Apply the
same argument to -u. This proves the lower-tail claim for the SAME
eta_u, with no need to choose a second coupling. Endpoints follow by
continuity; density domination ensures there are no hyperplane atoms. QED.

The measures eta_u can depend on u. Their full vector means, masses and
density ceilings do not. In particular

    y=[k g_K+a(g_A+g_B)]/(k+2a)                         (4)

is the centroid of 1_K dx+2eta_u for every u, and belongs to K. It is
therefore legitimate to choose the coupling separately when proving an
inequality for each halfspace through this ONE fixed y. It would not be
legitimate to integrate eta_u over several normal directions as though
it were one fixed measure. No such step is used here.

## 2. Exact same-tilt accounting

Let pi_u be the coupling of mass a on A x B used above. Its marginals
are 1_A dx and (a/b)1_B dx. For h,tau real set

    I_A=1{u.X>=h+tau},  I_B=1{u.Y>=h-tau},
    I_M=1{u.(X+Y)/2>=h},
    U_A=|A intersect{u.x>=h+tau}|,
    U_B=|B intersect{u.x>=h-tau}|.

Pointwise I_A+I_B-I_M is either zero or one. If neither endpoint is
captured, the midpoint is not captured; if both are captured, the
midpoint is captured. Consequently the following is an EXACT identity:

    U_A+U_B = eta_u{u.x>=h}+(1-a/b)U_B+E,
    E=integral(I_A+I_B-I_M) dpi_u >=0.                 (5)

This retains the unused larger-endpoint contribution at the SAME tau;
one cannot minimize the two terms on the right at different tilts.
The indicator identity includes all equality and support statuses.

When the two endpoint cuts and midpoint cut are proper, put

    p=U_A/a, q=U_B/b, m=eta_u{u.x>=h}/a.

Then the quantile identity and the paired thresholds give

    Q_A(p)+Q_B(q)=Q_A(m)+Q_B(m)=2h.                    (6)

In particular m lies between p and q. Since the two scalar endpoint
events are nested in the same uniform quantile parameter, their
intersection has pi_u-mass a min(p,q), and their union has mass
a max(p,q). Equation (5) may equivalently be written

    E=a(p+q-m),

including saturated statuses by the event formula, whether or not an
inverse-quantile threshold equality survives at a support endpoint.
This is additional actual-B information absent from an arbitrary
bounded-density eta. It is not by itself a proof of an asymmetric
depth guarantee at (4).

One elementary consequence of (3), useful for calibrating admissible
directional laws, is

    eta_u{u.x>=u.g_(eta_u)} >= Gamma_d a,
    eta_u{u.x<=u.g_(eta_u)} >= Gamma_d a.              (7)

Indeed q(r)=Q_eta(r^d) is concave, and the projected mean is
integral_0^1 q(r) d(r^d). Jensen gives mean<=q(d/(d+1)).
Because Q_eta is decreasing, its upper-tail probability at that mean
is at least (d/(d+1))^d. Reversal gives the other side. This proof
uses only the newly retained directional shape, not a claim that
eta_u itself is uniform on a convex body.

## 3. Exact all-tilt formula for cone projection profiles

Here is a finite directional subfamily in which (5)--(6) can be fully
optimized, including the discarded larger-endpoint contribution.
Suppose the endpoint upper quantiles are

    Q_A(p)=h_A-w_A p^(1/d),
    Q_B(p)=h_B-w_B p^(1/d),  0<=p<=1,                (8)

with w_A,w_B>0. Such marginals occur for cones with arbitrary
(d-1)-dimensional bases, with u pointing toward the respective apex.
No assertion that the full endpoint bodies are homothetic is needed.
Write m for the midpoint tail probability at any h in its support,
and put

    C_d=(w_A+w_B)^d /
        [w_A^(d/(d-1))a^(-1/(d-1))
          +w_B^(d/(d-1))b^(-1/(d-1))]^(d-1)          (d>1),
    C_1=(w_A+w_B) min(a/w_A,b/w_B).                  (d=1)

Then the EXACT minimum over all real tilts is

    min_tau [U_A+U_B] = min{a,C_d m}.                (9)

Proof for d>1. Define upper support deficits
delta_A=h_A-h-tau, delta_B=h_B-h+tau. From (2),(8),

    delta_A+delta_B=c=(w_A+w_B)m^(1/d),
    U_A+U_B=a clamp(delta_A/w_A,0,1)^d
              +b clamp(delta_B/w_B,0,1)^d.           (10)

Any state with at least one full endpoint has cost at least a. If
neither endpoint is full, put x=max(delta_A,0)/w_A,
y=max(delta_B,0)/w_B. Then w_A x+w_B y>=c. Sharp Holder gives
a x^d+b y^d>=C_d m. Thus every tilt costs at least the right side
of (9). A sufficiently large positive deficit for A makes A full and
B empty, realizing a exactly.

For the other branch minimize a x^d+b y^d over nonnegative x,y
with w_A x+w_B y=c. The unconstrained Holder equality minimizer
exists and has objective C_d m. If C_d m<a, its two nonnegative
summands are each less than a, so x<1 and y<(a/b)^(1/d)<=1.
It therefore corresponds to an actual proper pair of deficits and
realizes that branch. If C_d m=a, the full/empty realization already
suffices. Cases m=0,1 are covered directly by (10). This proves(9).

For d=1 the unsaturated cost is linear. Its minimum under
w_A x+w_B y>=c is c min(a/w_A,b/w_B)=C_1 m. If that value is
below a, the one-coordinate minimizing allocation is below its
corresponding upper constraint (cost<b as well). Otherwise the
full-A/empty-B allocation realizes a. The same lower-bound division
by full versus nonfull statuses applies. QED.

As a check, when w_A/w_B=(a/b)^(1/d), C_d=2v_*.
The full-A branch in (9) is essential, however: it prevents a false
uniform replacement of endpoint cost by 2v_* m. Thus even this
fully geometric transport family can lose all larger-endpoint credit
at the optimal tilt. The source must sometimes change.

## 4. Exact actual-body failure of the fixed source

This example was independently supplied by the parent calculation.
Let d=2, with continuous coordinates (x,t), and set

    K=B=conv{(0,0),(2,0),(0,1)},
    epsilon=1/100, P=(0,1),
    A=P+epsilon(K-P),  a=1/10000, k=b=1.

Let C be the convex hull of {-1}xA, {0}xK and {1}xB. Since A subset K=B,
the exact fibers at -1,0,1 are A,K,B; there are no other integer fibers.
C is a compact convex body in R^3, and (A+B)/2 subset K. All
three fibers have positive two-dimensional volume.

The midpoint body is M=P+(1+epsilon)(K-P)/2, and the affine homothety
transport realizes eta as the uniform-density measure (a/v_*)1_M dx.
In particular this eta obeys both tail-root constraints in every
direction, not merely the direction used below. The source (4) has
vertical coordinate

    g=166733/500100.

Take the ambient halfspace through that source

    H={ (z,x,t): t+(g-1)z>=g }.

At z=-1 its threshold is 2g-1=-83317/250050<0, so it captures all A.
At z=1 its threshold is 1, so it meets B only in its apex and captures
zero area. At z=0 it captures a K cap of area (1-g)^2. The total is

    |S intersect H|_MI=(1-g)^2+a
       =11115856669/25010001000,

whereas the requested n=1,d=2 target is

    (2/9)(2+a)=6667/15000.

The target minus the displayed cap is exactly

    159443/15631250625 >0.                             (11)

Thus the fixed source (4) fails the full asymmetric OC bound in an
actual compatible convex-body family, despite actual transport,
the sharper density ceiling, both directional concave tail roots,
and the SAME-tilt accounting. This is not a counterexample to OC:
for example this family lies in the independently proved nested-
endpoint regime. It only prohibits inferring the full result at
this one prescribed source from strengthened transport information.

## 5. Stronger preservation of the one-dimensional density shape

In fact, for d>=2 the normalized projected density of eta_u has
concave (d-1)-st root on its support. This is a ONE-dimensional
displacement interpolation statement. We prove it directly, without
assuming any corresponding d-dimensional preservation theorem.

Here is the general one-dimensional lemma. Let f_A,f_B be probability
densities, positive and continuous on bounded open support intervals,
and suppose f_A^p,f_B^p are concave there, for some p>0. Let Q_A,Q_B
now denote the INCREASING quantiles, and fix 0<=lambda<=1. The law
with increasing quantile

    Q=(1-lambda)Q_A+lambda Q_B                         (12)

has a positive continuous density f with f^p concave. Thus the
statement includes weights other than 1/2.

We first give an exact rank-coordinate characterization which also
handles nonsmooth concave roots. For one such density f let Q be its
increasing quantile, q=Q'=1/f(Q)>0, and put

    W=q^(-(p+1))=f(Q)^(p+1).

Then

    f^p is concave in the physical coordinate
       if and only if W is concave in the rank coordinate.             (13)

To prove the forward implication, write h=f^p. On every compact
subinterval of the support, h is positive and locally Lipschitz.
The quantile and its inverse are locally Lipschitz, with Q continuously
differentiable. Hence W is locally absolutely continuous and the
chain rule gives, at almost every rank t,

    W'(t)=(p+1)/p * h'(Q(t)).                         (14)

The a.e. derivative of a concave h has a nonincreasing representative.
Composition with the increasing Q is still nonincreasing; integrating
(14) proves concavity of W on (0,1). Every step is local, so possible
zero density or a positive facet density at a support endpoint causes
no regularity assumption.

Conversely, let W be positive concave on (0,1), put
q=W^(-1/(p+1)), and suppose its integral gives a finite increasing
quantile Q. The resulting density is f(Q)=1/q. On compact intervals
the same local absolute-continuity reasoning now gives

    d(f^p)/dx = p/(p+1) * W'(Q^(-1)(x))              (15)

almost everywhere. The right side has a nonincreasing representative,
so f^p is concave. This proves (13). Null exceptional sets are
preserved in both changes of variable because Q and its inverse are
Lipschitz on the compact intervals in question.

For (12), write r=-1/(p+1)<0. Its rank function is

    W=[(1-lambda)W_A^r+lambda W_B^r]^(1/r).           (16)

The function P_r(v,w) on the right is coordinatewise increasing and
concave for v,w>0. A direct calculation, with
S=(1-lambda)v^r+lambda w^r, gives its Hessian as

    (r-1)lambda(1-lambda) S^(1/r-2) v^(r-2)w^(r-2)
             * [[w^2,-vw],[-vw,v^2]].               (17)

The matrix displayed is positive semidefinite, and the scalar
coefficient is nonpositive. Its first partial derivatives are
nonnegative. The endpoint weights give the linear coordinate maps.
Applying concavity of W_A,W_B first, then monotonicity and concavity
of P_r, proves that W in (16) is concave. The reverse implication
of (13) proves the lemma. The integral of q is finite because q is
the convex combination of Q_A' and Q_B', each of which integrates
to its finite support length.

For a convex body in R^d, d>=2, the projected probability density
is its (d-1)-dimensional section volume divided by its volume and
the chosen coordinate normalization. Its (d-1)-st root is concave
by section Brunn--Minkowski, and its density is positive continuous
on the open support interval. Apply the lemma with p=1/(d-1) and
lambda=1/2 to the direction-adapted coupling from Section 1. It
follows that eta_u's directional density has that same section-root
concavity. When d=1, both endpoint bodies are intervals; their
comonotone midpoint law is uniform on an interval, which is the
separate interpretation in that dimension.

This gives a genuine directional convex-body marginal for every u,
in addition to all of (1),(5),(6). The full eta_u need not be uniform
on a convex body, and the collection of its laws for different u
is not asserted to be one common measure. The fixed-source failure
in Section 4 already has this stronger property, so a successful
global argument must still allow another actual center.

## 6. Uniform fixed-source obstruction in every d>=2

The preceding relocation calibration is not peculiar to the plane.
Let K=B be any volume-one d-simplex, d>=2, with apex P. Use its
affine height coordinate t, equal to one at P and zero on the
opposite facet. For

    0<epsilon<=1/(10d),    A=P+epsilon(K-P),
    a=epsilon^d,

form the same three-fiber convex hull A,K,B. The source (4) has
height

    g=[1+a(d+2-d epsilon)]/[(d+1)(1+2a)].             (18)

Its cap with B threshold one and A threshold 2g-1 has raw mass

    Q=Gamma_d [(1+a(1+epsilon))/(1+2a)]^d+a.

In fact the n=1 OC target exceeds this cap by the uniform amount

    Gamma_d(1+a/2)-Q >= 3a/50 >0.                    (19)

To check all statuses, a<=epsilon^2<=1/(100d^2)<=1/400, and
g<=1/(d+1)+2a<=1/3+1/200<1/2. Thus 2g-1<0, whereas every
point of A has height at least 1-epsilon>0; A is fully captured.
The closed B trace is its apex, of zero d-volume. The K trace is
proper and has volume (1-g)^d, which gives the displayed Q from
(18). As before the actual midpoint measure is constant-density
on a simplex, so all directional shape constraints are satisfied.

For the exact estimate, set s=a(1-epsilon)/(1+2a), in (0,1).
Twice integrating the inequality

    [1-(1-s)^d]''=-d(d-1)(1-s)^(d-2)>=-d(d-1)

gives 1-(1-s)^d>=ds-d(d-1)s^2/2. Therefore the deficit divided
by a is at least

    Gamma_d[1/2+d(1-epsilon)/(1+2a)
       -d(d-1)a(1-epsilon)^2/(2(1+2a)^2)]-1
      >=Gamma_d[d+1/2-d epsilon-2da-d^2 a/2]-1
      >=Gamma_d[d+77/200]-1.                         (20)

The second line uses (1-epsilon)/(1+2a)>=1-epsilon-2a.
The last uses d epsilon<=1/10, 2da<=1/100, and d^2 a/2<=1/200.
For d=2, Gamma_2=4/9 makes the last expression exactly 3/50.
For d>=3, Gamma_d>1/3 makes it greater than 77/600>3/50.
One elementary justification of Gamma_d>1/3 is the strict binomial
bound (1+1/d)^d<sum_(j>=0)1/j!<3; the latter follows from
1/j!<=1/2^(j-1) for j>=2, with strict inequality for j>=3.
This proves (19) without an asymptotic argument or a dimension
dependent unspecified smallness threshold.
